identity.name: Duchy of Lower Bavaria (House of Wittelsbach)

land.text: Lower Bavaria, Henry XIII's share in the partition of 1255: 'Henry received Lower Bavaria and Louis Upper Bavaria and the Palatinate' (Henry XIII page)

predecessors.note: The stem-duchy dossier ends in 1255 and names a successor 'duchy-of-lower-bavaria' that needs a dossier: this dossier (slug house-of-wittelsbach, Cliopatria's name for the row) is that state.

land.text: Lower Bavaria, inherited by Emperor Louis IV on the death of Duke John I in 1340, who reunited the duchy

successors.note: The duchy-of-bavaria dossier carries the matching gain of 1340.

capitals.name: Landshut
capitals.note: 'Henry resided in Landshut'; the Duchy of Bavaria page gives Lower Bavaria 'seats in Landshut and Burghausen' (Burghausen Castle begun 1255 per the Henry XIII page). No page opened calls either town the capital in so many words, and no year of the move to Landshut is given.

rulers.name: Henry XIII
rulers.note: Table: 29 Nov 1253 - 3 Feb 1290; his own page puts the partition in 1255 and gives 1253 (infobox) or 1254 (text) for his succession.

rulers.name: Otto III (jointly with Louis III to 1296 and Stephen I to 1310)
rulers.note: Table: 3 Feb 1290 - 9 Nov 1312, printed there as 'Otto V'; the Henry XIII page says he was succeeded by his oldest son Otto III, 'who also became King of Hungary'. Louis III 3 Feb 1290 - 13 May 1296, Stephen I 3 Feb 1290 - 10 Dec 1310 in the table.

rulers.name: Henry XIV the Elder (jointly with Otto IV, d. 1334)
rulers.note: Table: 9 Nov 1312 - 1 Sep 1339; the Henry XIV page gives 'Reign: 1310-1339'.

correction.text: the 1260 outline carried back to the partition of 1255: 'Henry received Lower Bavaria and Louis Upper Bavaria and the Palatinate'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1255-1259: Cliopatria's row starts in 1260. 'The brothers divided their land in 1255 against the law.' The House of Wittelsbach page dates the division to 1253 (Otto II's death) and its family tree gives 'Divided in Upper and Lower Bavaria in 1253-1340'; the Duchy of Bavaria page, like this one, says 1255.

18.2 k km2 for 1260-1271. By its outline (bbox 11.0-13.7 E, 47.6-49.3 N) the row is the east of Bavaria, Landshut and Burghausen with the Inn-Salzach side; Munich lies outside it, as the page's 'Upper Bavaria with the Palatinate and the Nordgau (headquartered in Munich) and Lower Bavaria (with seats in Landshut and Burghausen)' requires. No page opened gives a boundary or an area for Lower Bavaria, so the extent is unverified beyond that.
18.23 k km2, +0.07 k km2 on the 1260 outline; no page opened dates a boundary change here.
17.80 k km2, -0.43 k km2 on 1272 (-2%); no page opened dates the change, so the outline stands as Cliopatria's approximation.
17.69 k km2 for 1294-1325, -0.11 k km2 on 1279; the same bounding box throughout. No page opened dates the change.
Same 17.69 k km2 outline for 1326-1332, the last year of Cliopatria's row. Lower Bavaria went on under Henry XIV ('Reign: 1310-1339') and his son John I; see the new keyframe 1333-1340.

correction.text: Lower Bavaria unchanged, under Henry XIV until his death on 1 September 1339 and under John I until 1340

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1333-1340: Cliopatria's row ends in 1332. The Henry XIV page: 'Some months after the reconciliation with Louis IV in February 1339 Henry died' and 'was succeeded by his son John I'; the House of Wittelsbach table ends John I on 20 Dec 1340. Lower Bavaria is therefore not 'nobody's' in 1333-1339, as the duchy-of-bavaria dossier assumed.

region.text: Lower Bavaria, Henry XIII's half of the partitioned Wittelsbach land

ledger.note: 1255: the Wittelsbach brothers divide Bavaria and Henry XIII takes Lower Bavaria. 'The brothers divided their land in 1255 against the law.' 'Henry received Lower Bavaria and Louis Upper Bavaria and the Palatinate.' The page names the duchy, not a boundary; the outline is Cliopatria's 1260 row.

1340: Lower Bavaria passes to Emperor Louis IV. 'With the death of duke John I in 1340 Louis inherited Lower Bavaria.' The House of Wittelsbach page: 'Emperor Louis IV had reunited Bavaria in 1340'; its table ends John I's reign on 20 Dec 1340.

region.text: Lower Bavaria, reunited with Upper Bavaria

ledger.note: 1340: the Lower Bavarian line dies out and the duchy is reunited. 'Henry's branch died out in 1340 and was inherited by Louis' son Emperor Louis IV' (the page's wording; the Louis IV page says Louis IV himself inherited).

wars.name: Ottokar II's invasion of Bavaria (1257)
wars.outcome: Repulsed: 'In August 1257, Ottokar invaded Bavaria, but Henry and Louis managed to repulse the attack.'
wars.note: The page says the bishops allied with Ottokar in 1257. It also says Henry was 'several times at war' with Salzburg and Passau and 'repeatedly changed allegiance' in Rudolph I's conflict with Ottokar II, with no dates, so no further war is entered and no border moved.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary of Lower Bavaria; the outline is Cliopatria's approximation of the duchy's lands from Landshut and Burghausen.

notes:
WHAT THIS ROW IS. Cliopatria's 'House of Wittelsbach' (1260-1332, 5 shapes, 17.7-18.2 k km2) is, by its outline, the east of Bavaria: Lower Bavaria, the share of Henry XIII in the Wittelsbach partition of 1255. The duchy-of-bavaria dossier reads it the same way, and the stem-duchy-of-bavaria dossier names a successor 'duchy-of-lower-bavaria' that needs a dossier: this dossier is that state, kept under Cliopatria's slug. The state is not the House of Wittelsbach (which also ruled Upper Bavaria, the Palatinates, Brandenburg, Tyrol and Holland in these years); the display name says so.

WHAT I EXTENDED. Start 1255 (the partition: Henry XIII page 1255; House of Wittelsbach page 1253; Duchy of Bavaria page 1255) and end Dec 1340 (John I's reign ends 20 Dec 1340 in the House of Wittelsbach table; Louis IV inherits in 1340) instead of Cliopatria's 1260-1332, with two new keyframes that repeat the nearest Cliopatria outline. Between 1333 and 1339 the duchy was ruled by Henry XIV (reign to 1 September 1339) and then John I, so it was not stateless as the duchy-of-bavaria dossier's notes assume.

NOT SETTLED. (a) No page opened gives a boundary or an area for Lower Bavaria; the small changes in 1272, 1279 and 1294 (-2% in all) are not dated by any page and are left as ok. (b) The Louis IV page says at Pavia (1329) Louis 'inherited both Upper and Lower Bavaria for himself' and that Lower Bavaria came to him in 1340; the Henry XIV and House of Wittelsbach pages show Henry XIV and John I ruling Lower Bavaria until 1339-1340, so the dated 1340 inheritance is used. (c) The House of Wittelsbach ruler table prints 'Otto V' for the Lower Bavarian duke who ruled 1290-1312; the Henry XIII and Louis IV pages call him Otto III, King of Hungary, and that name is used. Henry XIV's own page gives 1310 as the start of his reign, the table 9 Nov 1312. (d) Henry XIII's wars with Salzburg and Passau, undated on his page, are not entered. (e) Which towns belong to Lower Bavaria is not on any page opened; Straubing is never called a seat. Gazetteer: no new names used (Cliopatria regions only).
